corrections.subject: Range Onset timeframe
corrections.previous_ambiguity: The provider config names a one-minute input timeframe, which could be read as a one-minute entry strategy.
corrections.corrected_position: The provider consumes completed one-minute bars, but its native onset is an hourly SMA10/SMA30 crossover followed by a five-minute context check. Its opportunity cadence is therefore hourly and sparse, not a one-minute growth cadence.
corrections.falsifier: The production signal builder or exact provider ledger shows an eligible entry that was not caused by a completed hourly SMA crossover.

corrections.subject: Canary-to-$5K promotion discipline
corrections.previous_ambiguity: A repaired forward experiment was treated as eligible for a full-sized v51 route despite insufficient compatible live outcomes.
corrections.corrected_position: A sparse experimental route must not receive a full-size growth slot merely because historical partitions are positive. Compatible live translation, exact costs, and exit behavior are required before material sizing.
corrections.confidence: high on the process defect; low on universal future expectancy
corrections.falsifier: A predeclared compatible live window produces stable positive after-cost outcomes across independent episodes and both configured directions without largest-winner dependence.

single_highest_value_next_investigation: Determine the smallest fail-closed transition that blocks new Range Onset entries without orphaning the existing SOL stop or changing unrelated v51 routes, then identify a distinct lower-timeframe ETH/SOL replacement.
Recommendation: Retire Range Onset from new ETH and SOL entries at the next technically safe transition boundary; preserve the existing SOL venue stop and frozen exit plan until native resolution unless the user separately authorizes a manual close.
Why now: The route was explicitly an experimental, sparse hourly-cross mechanism, yet received approximately $500 margin per entry in the $5K run. Two resolved compatible ETH longs lost and the first SOL lifecycle is marked negative.
Evidence reviewed: Exact v51 six-close archive, open-lifecycle reflections, prior compatible ETH canary audit, v49 repair disposition, ETH/SOL live-translation journals, index translation journal, BRENTOIL canary reconciliation, top-ten liquidity audit, and mutable BRENTOIL/MU observer status.
Observed problem or opportunity: A low-confidence forward experiment crossed into material sizing without adequate compatible live outcomes. The resulting route consumes two asset slots while offering sparse hourly opportunities and no demonstrated live winner.
Applicable market regime: No universal regime restriction is claimed. The decision is based on live translation and portfolio-role mismatch, not a claim that the route fails in every regime.
Alternatives considered: Do nothing and await more material Range Onset trades: rejected because it repeats the promotion error with real capital.
Retune Range Onset immediately: rejected as circular research without a new causal mechanism.
Close the current SOL position immediately: not proposed automatically because its venue stop and native exit plan are intact and manual closure requires separate explicit approval.
Block new Range Onset entries and research a distinct lower-timeframe replacement: recommended.
Proposed live change: After explicit approval and a verified safe transition procedure, disable new range_onset_bidirectional_v1 entries for ETH and SOL while preserving management of the existing SOL lifecycle; leave BTC, HYPE, SP500, and SPCX routes unchanged.
Expected upside: Prevents another unvalidated approximately $500-margin / $5,000-notional hourly experiment, frees two roster roles for higher-frequency candidates, and reduces process risk. No profit amount is forecast.
Main risks and failure modes: The small live sample may reject a rare-winner mechanism too early.
Removing ETH and SOL routes reduces opportunity frequency until replacements qualify.
A careless config transition could orphan the existing SOL exit plan or duplicate orders.
A replacement strategy can also fail unless subjected to stricter live-translation rules.
Validation completed: Reconciled six current-epoch closes and two protected open positions.
Verified hourly crossover semantics in the production signal builder.
Reconciled two resolved compatible ETH Range Onset losses under distinct exits.
Verified the current SOL lifecycle has an armed venue stop.
Reviewed historical counterevidence and its largest-winner/partition limitations.
Validation still required: Prove the transition blocks new Range Onset entries while retaining the current SOL controller and stop.
Require fresh venue/ledger/order reconciliation at the transition boundary.
Run targeted routing, restart-adoption, stop-ownership, accounting, and TUI tests.
Qualify any replacement with point-in-time data, realistic friction, chronological OOS evidence, and a bounded live canary before material sizing.
Success metrics: No new ETH or SOL Range Onset entry after the approved transition.
The existing SOL lifecycle closes once with no orphan or duplicate order.
Unrelated v51 routes retain exact identity and behavior.
Replacement candidates demonstrate positive after-cost OOS and compatible live translation before material sizing.
Failure / rollback triggers: The transition cannot preserve the existing SOL plan and stop.
Any removed route continues generating executable intents.
Any rollback is attempted while positions or owned orders make it unsafe.
Confidence level: High on the promotion-discipline defect and poor roster fit; medium that retirement prevents further loss; low on claiming universal negative strategy expectancy from two ETH closes and one unresolved SOL lifecycle.
limitations: This revision is report-only and changes no live route, position, order, parameter, sizing, leverage, exit, or deployment state.
The exact current SOL and SPCX outcomes remain unresolved and can change after this snapshot.
Two ETH losses do not establish universal negative expectancy, but they invalidate material promotion without further compatible evidence.
Mutable observer and checkpoint status continues to advance beyond the cited observation times.
